 Medicare Open Enrollment Allows Retirees to Make Changes to Plans
 By Tom Robinson 
 Oct 18, 2026 | 4:03 AM 
 (NAFB News Service) One of the most closely watched Social Security announcements each year is the next cost-of-living adjustment, or COLA. Sean Voskuhl, the Oklahoma State AARP Director, said Social Security benefits receive a COLA to help older adults keep up with inflation. 
 https://media-cdn.socastsrm.com/wordpress/wp-content/blogs.dir/2424/files/2026/10/n-1018-2-voskuhl.mp3   AARP has conducted research to understand whether adults age 50-plus believe the projected COLA is sufficient. 
 https://media-cdn.socastsrm.com/wordpress/wp-content/blogs.dir/2424/files/2026/10/n-1018-3-voskuhl.mp3   Voskuhl said do not forget that Medicare Open Enrollment runs October 15-December 7. Voskuhl says during the window, people with Medicare can review and make several changes. They can join, drop, or switch to a Medicare Advantage plan (Part C) with or without prescription drug coverage. You can switch from Original Medicare (Parts A and B) to a Medicare Advantage Plan, or vice versa. You can also join, drop, or switch a standalone Medicare Part D prescription drug plan. ”
